content: Tolnaftate is an over-the-counter antifungal medication that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of athlete’s foot (tinea pedis) and ringworm (tinea corporis). It is also used to provide relief from symptoms such as itching, burning, and cracking of the skin. For adults, the affected area should be washed and dried thoroughly before application. A thin layer of the medication should be applied to the affected area twice daily, once in the morning and once at night. When treating athlete’s foot, special attention should be given to the spaces between the toes. Patients are advised to wear well-fitting, ventilated shoes and to change their shoes and socks at least once daily. The treatment should be continued daily for four weeks. If the condition persists beyond this period, a healthcare provider should be consulted. To prevent athlete’s foot, the medication can be applied once or twice daily, either in the morning or at night. It is important to note that this product is not effective for fungal infections of the scalp or nails. Children using this product should be supervised. There is limited information available regarding off-label uses of Tolnaftate in adults, but it has been mentioned in the context of onychomycosis caused by dermatophytes. Similarly, there is limited information regarding its use in pediatric patients, both for FDA-labeled and off-label indications. Tolnaftate is contraindicated for use in children under the age of 2 unless directed by a healthcare provider. It is intended for external use only and should not come into contact with the eyes. If irritation occurs or if there is no improvement within four weeks, the use of the product should be discontinued, and a healthcare provider should be consulted. In the event of accidental ingestion, medical help or contact with a Poison Control Center is advised immediately. The most commonly reported adverse reaction associated with Tolnaftate is irritation. There is limited information available regarding postmarketing experiences, drug interactions, and specific population use, including during pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing, pediatric, geriatric, gender, race, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, and immunocompromised patients. Tolnaftate is administered as a topical cream. It should be stored at a temperature of 68°-77°F (20°-25°C). There is no established interaction between Tolnaftate and alcohol, but patients are advised to consult their healthcare provider regarding alcohol use while taking this medication. The product is marketed under the brand name Tinactin® and is labeled as effective for curing most cases of athlete’s foot and relieving associated symptoms such as itching and burning. The active ingredient in the cream is Tolnaftate USP, 1%.
